criterion: ROADMAP P11 and coordinator round 2 item 2 (2026-10-21): a sunlit arched colonnade with the sky model, mirror and rough spheres and an emissive sphere, at noon, golden hour and sunset; a compact test of soft shadows, colour bleed and the sky. Stage 1 here: the path-traced scene, its reference images, checks and CPU frame times, and command-line settings. Stage 2: a live settings panel in the Studio (it needs a GPU path for the v3 scene) and a raster comparison.
written: 2026-10-21, before any colonnade code and before any run

design.scene: raw/renderer/rt_colonnade.hpp, src/renderer/rt_colonnade.cpp: a stone floor, a terracotta back wall, six marble columns carrying five semicircular arches and an entablature, a near-mirror sphere, a rough copper sphere and a small warm emissive sphere, all of our own geometry and path tracer v3 full materials. The sky is sky::preetham baked into the v3 environment (no disk); the sun is a v3 directional light along the sky's sun with sky::sunIlluminance.
design.command: raw_native_cli colonnade [--out DIR] [--width W --height H] [--spp N] [--sun-elev DEG] [--sun-az DEG] [--turbidity T] [--ev EV100] [--no-emission] [--threads T]: the settings a stage-2 panel will expose

co1_sky.what: pixels whose camera ray escapes (no triangle) against the environment sampled along the same ray
co1_sky.prediction: holds: an escaped camera ray takes the environment with weight 1

co2_colour_bleed.what: red over blue luminance of a floor patch beside the emissive sphere, emission on against off, sunset

co3_shadow.what: luminance of a floor patch in a column's sun shadow over a sunlit patch nearby, golden hour
co3_shadow.prediction: holds; the sky fills the shadow

co4_regression.what: tests/test_colonnade.cpp: the path tracer's frame of the scene at 64 x 36, 4 samples, hashed per compiler family (GCC, MSVC)

co5_frame_times.what: CPU path tracer wall time per sample per pixel at 480 x 270, 8 bounces, noon, golden hour and sunset
co5_frame_times.prediction: a few microseconds a sample a pixel on 4 threads

co6_review.bound: shadows soft at golden hour and sunset, the arches' shadows on the wall, the sphere's warm bleed on the floor, the sky's colour changing with the sun; recorded

does_not_prove: Real-time rates (CPU only here); agreement with a raster (stage 2); that the sky matches a measured one.

addendum_A.written: 2026-10-21, after the first test run, before any recorded run; no bound changed
addendum_A.what_was_seen: co3 misses on the first run: golden-hour floor in a column's sun shadow 2,934 nits against 4,384 sunlit, ratio 0.669 (bound 0.5). With the sun 10 degrees up, its illuminance on a horizontal floor is about sin(10 deg) = 0.17 of its normal value, so the sky lights the floor more than the sun does and a shadow only removes a third of the light. My prediction ignored the cosine.
addendum_A.what_changes: co3 stays as written and is recorded as a miss; the test prints it without failing on it. The shadow is right for the physics; the bound was wrong for this sun.
